data.one_liner: Executes async tasks with a configurable maximum concurrency and rate.
data.what_it_does: Executes asynchronous tasks while strictly respecting a configurable maximum concurrency limit and rate. Provides methods for scheduling tasks, tracking running or waiting counts, and joining execution blocks.
use_when: You need to limit concurrent asynchronous operations like network requests or database writes.
You want to control the execution rate of a batch of asynchronous tasks.
avoid_when: You are looking for the Dart team's pool library and prefer that specific ecosystem alternative.
You do not have any concurrency or rate-limiting requirements for your async tasks.
strengths: Supports joining execution with waiting options.
Preserves caller stacktraces when tasks fail.
weaknesses: Limited feature set beyond basic async scheduling and rate control.

alternatives.name: async
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers general asynchronous tools and utilities maintained directly by the Dart team.
